back: A cost that does not change with output in the short run and must be paid even at zero output (rent, insurance, loan interest).
A cost that changes directly with output and is zero at zero output (raw materials, fuel, packaging, piece-rate wages).
A cost with a fixed part and a variable part, such as a phone bill with a monthly fee plus a charge per call.
ATC = TC ÷ output; AFC = TFC ÷ output; AVC = TVC ÷ output; ATC = AFC + AVC.

front: What happens to average fixed cost as output rises?
back: It falls continuously, because the same fixed cost is spread over more units.
U-shaped: falls as fixed costs are spread and resources are used better, then rises as fixed factors become crowded (diminishing returns).
The period in which at least one factor of production is fixed, so the firm has fixed and variable costs.
The period in which all factors of production can be changed, so all costs are variable.
